st: Season the chicken with [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Brown the chicken for 4 minutes per side, then set aside.
Cook the onion in the same pot for 5 minutes until soft. Add the garlic, tomatoes, and chili and cook 5 more minutes.
Return the chicken to the pot and add [[2 cups]] water. Cover and simmer for 20 minutes.
Pour in the palm nut cream and [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Stir well, which will turn the sauce orange-red.
Simmer uncovered on low heat for 45 minutes, stirring often, until the oil rises to the top and the sauce thickens.
Check that the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C) and is tender. Add a little water if the sauce is too thick.
Serve hot with rice, cassava, or plantains.
Wear gloves and peel the cassava, cut into chunks, and remove the woody center core.
Cover the chunks with water in a large bowl and soak for 3 days at room temperature until slightly sour, changing the water daily. For a quicker version, soak 2 hours.
Rinse the cassava well, then boil it for 20 minutes to make it safe to eat. Drain.
Mash or process the softened cassava into a thick, smooth dough. Mix in [[1 tsp]] salt.
Warm the banana leaves over a flame or hot water for a few seconds so they stay flexible. If using foil, skip this.
Shape about [[0.5 cup]] dough into a stick, roll it tightly in a leaf, and tie or fold the ends shut. Repeat.
Set a rack in a large pot with 2 inches of water. Stack the sticks on the rack.
Cover and steam for 60 minutes, adding hot water if needed.
Cool for 10 minutes, unwrap, and slice. Serve with sauces or stews.

ing: frozen, thawed, or fresh and finely chopped
st: If using fresh cassava leaves, chop them very finely or pound them. Rinse thawed leaves in cold water.
Boil the leaves in [[3 cups]] water for 30 minutes until tender. Drain and press out extra water.
Heat [[0.25 cup]] palm oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion and garlic for 5 minutes.
Add the leaves and stir well for 3 minutes.
Stir [[0.5 cup]] peanut butter with a ladle of hot water to loosen it, then add it to the pot with the fish, chili, and [[1 tsp]] salt.
Cover and simmer on low for 30 minutes, stirring often to prevent sticking. Add water by the splash if it dries out.
Taste and add salt if needed. Serve with rice, plantains, or cassava sticks.

ing: wild mango seed paste, or smooth peanut butter plus 1 tbsp cocoa
st: Chop the onion and mince the chili and garlic.
Bring [[1.5 cups]] water to a gentle simmer in a medium pot. Add the onion, garlic, and chili and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the fish chunks and [[1 tsp]] salt. Poach for 6 minutes until the fish is opaque.
Lift the fish out onto a plate and keep it warm.
Whisk [[0.5 cup]] odika paste with a ladle of the hot liquid to make a smooth cream.
Pour the paste back into the pot and stir on low heat for 10 minutes until the sauce is thick and glossy. Do not boil hard.
Return the fish to the sauce and warm for 3 minutes. Serve with cassava or rice.
Cut the ends off the plantains and slice through the skin lengthwise. Peel it off with your fingers.
Slice the plantains on a slant into pieces about 0.5 inch thick.
Pour [[0.5 cup]] oil into a large skillet and heat over medium heat until a plantain slice sizzles right away.
Add a single layer of slices, leaving space between them.
Fry for 3 minutes on the first side until deep golden brown.
Flip and fry for 2 minutes more on the other side until caramelized at the edges.
Move to a paper towel to drain, sprinkle with a pinch of salt if you like, and fry the next batch.
Mix [[3 cups]] flour, [[0.33 cup]] sugar, [[2.25 tsp]] yeast, and [[0.5 tsp]] salt in a large bowl.
Add [[1 cup]] warm water and the egg. Stir to a soft, sticky dough, then knead for 5 minutes.
Cover the bowl and let the dough rise in a warm place for 60 minutes until doubled.
Pour [[3 cups]] oil into a heavy pot, at least 3 inches deep, and heat to 350°F (175°C).
Wet your hand and scoop golf ball-sized pieces of dough, dropping them gently into the oil.
Fry in small batches for 3 minutes, turning, until puffy and golden all over.
Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
Let cool for 5 minutes before eating. Break one open to check it is cooked through.
